page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM hypervisor virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The system includes 16.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks bundled local NVMe SSD storage and relies entirely on external block storage, backed by a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions.

Benchmark results indicate single-core CPU capabilities in the top 25% cohort, demonstrated by high scores in single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench single-core execution, and text processing workloads. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench software compilation, and PassMark tests falls within the middle 50% average range. Static web serving throughput at 11.45 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 11.11 million operations per second similarly align with average benchmark tiers. The instance delivers strong single-threaded instruction processing, though its overall multi-threaded throughput is bounded by its 4 physical core count.

Without bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, the ecs.c8a.2xlarge maintains a lean resource footprint focused primarily on CPU execution. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a resource-efficient allocation for workloads that prioritize single-thread CPU performance over large in-memory footprints. This profile fits web serving, moderate software compilation, microservices, and general compute-bound workloads that leverage vector extensions without requiring high-density memory.
